small.label: supported
small.says: Delos is a small island near Mykonos, close to the center of the Cyclades, and one of the most important mythological, historical and archaeological sites in Greece.
quote: is a small Greek island near Mykonos, close to the centre of the Cyclades archipelago.
it is one of the most important mythological, historical, and archaeological sites in Greece.

unesco.label: verified
unesco.says: UNESCO inscribed Delos on the World Heritage List in 1990.
quote: Date of Inscription: 1990
In 1990, UNESCO added Delos to the World Heritage List

whole-site.label: verified
whole-site.says: The entire island is an archaeological site.
quote: Nowadays, the entire island is designated as an archaeological site.

nobody.label: supported
nobody.says: Overnight stays are forbidden; the only inhabitants are security staff and archaeologists.
quote: Overnight stay on Delos is forbidden. The only "inhabitants" of the island are security personnel and archaeologists.

sun.label: supported
sun.says: There is no protection from the sun on the island; bring plenty of water.
quote: Be aware there is no protection from the sun on the island so take the usual precautions.
Bring plenty of water.

mounds.label: disputed
mounds.says: From the Sacred Harbor you can see three conical mounds that marked landscapes sacred to a goddess, presumably Athena.
quote: From its Sacred Harbour are visible the three conical mounds that have identified landscapes sacred to a goddess (presumably Athena).

agora.label: supported
agora.says: The Agora of the Competaliasts, by the Sacred Harbor, still has the postholes for market awnings in its paving.
quote: The Hellenistic Agora of the Competaliasts by the Sacred Harbour retains the postholes for market awnings in its stone paving.

settled.label: verified
settled.says: The island was first settled in the third millennium BC.
quote: The island was first settled in the third millennium BC.
it has been inhabited since the third millennium BC

sanctuary.label: verified
sanctuary.says: Apollo's sanctuary existed at least from the 9th century BC and peaked in the Archaic and Classical periods, when it became Pan-Hellenic.
quote: The Apollonian sanctuary, established at least since the 9th century BC, reached the peak of its glory during the Archaic and Classical period, when it acquired its Pan-Hellenic character.

pilgrims.label: verified
pilgrims.says: Apollo's sanctuary drew pilgrims from all over Greece, and Delos was a prosperous trading port.
quote: Apollo's sanctuary attracted pilgrims from all over Greece and Delos was a prosperous trading port.

three-temples.label: supported
three-temples.says: There are three temples dedicated to Apollo.
quote: The temples of Apollo: the three temples dedicated to Apollo;

kouros.label: supported
kouros.says: Beside the Temple of the Delians stood a colossal kouros of Apollo from the 6th century BC; parts of the torso and pelvis remain in place, a hand is in the local museum and a foot in the British Museum.
quote: The Temple of the Delians, dedicated to Apollo, is a classic example of the Doric order. Beside the temple, once stood a colossal kouros of Apollo, only parts of which remain. Dating to the sixth century BC, parts of the upper torso and pelvis remain in situ, a hand is kept at the local museum, and a foot is in the British Museum.

feast.label: verified
feast.says: The feast of the Delians was held every four years in May until 316 BC, with athletic, horse and music contests, dances, plays and banquets.
quote: The feast of the Delians, which was celebrated every four years in the month of May until 316 BC, included gymnastic, equestrian and musical competitions, Archaic Age dances, theatrical productions and banquets.

league-what.label: supported
league-what.says: The Delian League was an alliance of between 150 and 330 Greek city-states, founded in 478 BC under Athenian leadership, to keep fighting Persia.
quote: The Delian League was a confederacy of Greek city-states, numbering between 150 and 330, founded in 478 BC under the hegemony of Athens, whose purpose was to continue fighting the Persian Empire

league-here.label: supported
league-here.says: Its congresses were held here in the temple, and its common treasury was kept here until 454 BC, when Pericles moved it to Athens.
quote: the congresses being held in the temple
The league's common treasury was kept here as well until 454 BC, when Pericles removed it to Athens.

league-iron.label: supported
league-iron.says: Members swore to have the same friends and enemies, and dropped iron ingots into the sea to show the alliance was permanent.
quote: League members swore to have the same friends and enemies, and dropped ingots of iron into the sea to symbolize the permanence of their alliance.

league-money.label: supported
league-money.says: Athens used the funds for its navy and to embellish the city with art and architecture; the league became known as the Athenian Empire.
quote: Athens used the money to reinforce its own naval supremacy and used the remaining funds to embellish the city with art and architecture.
conventionally called the Athenian Empire

purify.label: supported
purify.says: In the 6th century BC Pisistratus had graves in sight of the temple dug up and moved; in the fifth century BC the whole island was cleared of the dead, and a decree barred anyone from being buried or giving birth here.
quote: A number of "purifications" were performed by the city-state of Athens
These first took place in the 6th century BC, directed by the tyrant Pisistratus, who ordered that all graves within sight of the temple be dug up and the bodies moved to another nearby island.
In the fifth century BC, during the sixth year of the Peloponnesian War and under instruction from the Delphic Oracle, the entire island was purged of all dead bodies.
so that no one should be allowed to be buried or give birth on the island due to its sacred importance

rhenia.label: supported
rhenia.says: A narrow channel separates Delos from Rhenia, where there is an important burial ground.
quote: A narrow channel separates Delos from the island of Rhenia, where there is an important burial ground.

necropolis.label: supported
necropolis.says: The necropolis of Delos was on Rhenia in Classical and Hellenistic times.
quote: The necropolis of Delos was located on Rhenia during Classical and Hellenistic times.

lions.label: supported
lions.says: The people of Naxos dedicated the Terrace of the Lions to Apollo shortly before 600 BC; it once had 9 to 12 crouching, snarling marble lions along the Sacred Way.
quote: The Terrace of the Lions, also was dedicated to Apollo by the people of Naxos shortly before 600 BC. It originally had 9–12 squatting, snarling marble guardian lions along the Sacred Way

lions-seven.label: supported
lions-seven.says: Today only seven of the original lions remain.
quote: Today, only seven of the original lions remain.

lions-arsenal.label: supported
lions-arsenal.says: One lion was taken away and now stands over the main gate of the Venetian Arsenal.
quote: one was removed and is presently situated over the main gate of the Venetian Arsenal.

lions-sphinx.label: supported
lions-sphinx.says: The lions form a monumental avenue like the Egyptian avenues of sphinxes.
quote: The lions create a monumental avenue comparable to Egyptian avenues of sphinxes.

lions-replicas.label: verified
lions-replicas.says: Because the north wind could damage them, the marble Naxian Lions were moved into the museum and replaced outside with exact replicas.
quote: Because of potential damage by the north wind, fragile marble sculptures, such as the Naxian Lions, were transported to the Museum and have been replaced with exact replicas.
There is a set of large lion statues which are originals; of those reproduced outside on the Delos site.

myth-leto.label: legend
myth-leto.says: In myth, Leto, pregnant by Zeus and fleeing Hera's vengeance, gave birth to Apollo and Artemis here after a difficult labor.
quote: It was on this arid islet that Leto, made pregnant by Zeus and fleeing the vengeance of Hera, gave birth to Apollo and Artemis after a difficult labour.

myth-shun.label: legend
myth-shun.says: In the myth, jealous Hera ordered all lands to refuse Leto shelter; Delos, not joined to the mainland or the sea floor, did not count as land.
quote: Hera, the wife of Zeus, in her jealousy, ordered all lands to shun her and deny her shelter.
Leto eventually found an island, Delos, that was not joined to the mainland or attached to the ocean floor, therefore it was not considered land or island and she could give birth.

myth-lake.label: legend
myth-lake.says: In the myth, Leto suffered labor pains for nine days and nights close to the wheel-shaped lake.
quote: the wheel-shaped lake, close to which the pregnant Leto suffered labor pains for nine days and nights

myth-eileithyia.label: legend
myth-eileithyia.says: In the Homeric Hymn, Eileithyia, goddess of childbirth, was kept away with Hera on Olympus; on the ninth day Iris won her over with a necklace and brought her to Delos.
quote: Only Eileithyia, the goddess of childbirth, was not present; she, unaware of the situation, was with jealous Hera on Olympus.
Then, on the ninth day, Eileithyia was sent for by the messenger goddess Iris, who persuaded her with a necklace and brought her to Delos.

myth-anchor.label: legend
myth-anchor.says: A Homeric hymn says the island, floating until then, became anchored to the ocean floor; the newborn Apollo threw off his swaddling clothes, bathed the universe in light and began walking with his lyre and bow.
quote: According to a Homeric hymn, the island, which until then had been floating, became anchored to the floor of the ocean.
The newborn Phoebus- Apollo threw off his swaddling clothes bathed the universe in light and began walking with his cither and his bow.

myth-versions.label: legend
myth-versions.says: Versions differ: some say Artemis was born on Ortygia before Apollo was born on Delos, and a local tradition put Apollo's birth at Tegyra in Boeotia.
quote: Artemis was born on the island of Ortygia before Apollo was on Delos.
According to a local tradition, Apollo was not born on Delos at all, but in Tegyra, a town in Boeotia

lake-dry.label: supported
lake-dry.says: The small sacred lake in its round bowl is now deliberately kept dry by the caretakers to stop malaria mosquitoes.
quote: The small sacred lake in its circular bowl, now intentionally left dry by the island's caretakers to suppress the spread of malaria-bearing mosquitoes

free-port.label: verified
free-port.says: After 167 BC Delos was declared a free port, and the trade of the eastern Mediterranean concentrated here; rich merchants, bankers and ship-owners settled and built luxurious houses with frescoes and mosaic floors.
quote: After 167 BC, as a result of the declaration of Delos as a free port, all the commercial activity of the eastern Mediterranean was concentrated on the isle.

Rich merchants, bankers and ship-owners from all over the world settled there, attracting many builders, artists and craftsmen, who built for them luxurious houses, richly decorated with frescoes and mosaic floors.

greatest.label: verified
greatest.says: The ancient writer Festus called it the greatest commercial center of the whole world.
quote: the greatest commercial centre of the whole world

slaves.label: supported
slaves.says: Roman traders bought tens of thousands of slaves here; Delos became the center of the slave trade, with the largest slave market in the wider region.
quote: Roman traders came to purchase tens of thousands of slaves
It became the centre of the slave trade, with the largest slave market in the larger region being maintained here.

dionysus-house.label: supported
dionysus-house.says: The House of Dionysus is a luxurious private house named for its floor mosaic of Dionysus riding a panther; the House of the Dolphins is named for its mosaic of erotes riding dolphins.
quote: The House of Dionysus is a luxurious second-century private house named for the floor mosaic of Dionysus riding a panther.
The House of the Dolphins is similarly named from its atrium mosaic, where erotes ride dolphins

foreign-gods.label: verified
foreign-gods.says: There were many sanctuaries of foreign religions: temples of Sarapis, Isis and Anubis, of Syrian gods, and even a synagogue in the stadium district.
quote: there were an unprecedented number of sanctuaries dedicated to foreign religions: temples of Sarapis, Isis and Anubis, temples to the Syrian gods Haadad and Atargatis, and even a synagogue in the stadium district.

synagogue.label: disputed
synagogue.says: The so-called Delos Synagogue was once believed to be an ancient Samaritan synagogue.
quote: The "Delos Synagogue", the ruins of what was once believed to be an ancient Samaritan synagogue.

samaritans.label: supported
samaritans.says: Inscriptions record a community calling itself 'Israelites on Delos' who made offerings to Mount Gerizim.
quote: the community identified itself as "Israelites on Delos who make offerings to hallowed Argarizein," a clear reference to Mount Gerizim

herod.label: supported
herod.says: Delos is where an inscription honoring Herod the Great, King of Judaea, was found, and another honoring his son Herod Antipas.
quote: Delos is also the findspot of an inscription honoring Herod the Great, King of Judaea, as well as another honoring his son, the tetrarch Herod Antipas

museum.label: supported
museum.says: The museum holds many statues from the site, though a large quantity of finds are in the National Archaeological Museum in Athens.
quote: It is noted for its extensive collection of statues unearthed in the surrounding area of the ancient site
a large quantity are on display in Athens at the National Archaeological Museum.

sack.label: verified
sack.says: Delos was attacked and looted twice, in 88 BC by Mithridates and in 69 BC by the pirates of Athenodorus; then it declined and was gradually abandoned.
quote: Delos was attacked and looted twice: in 88 BC by Mithridates, the King of Pontus, an enemy of the Romans, and later, in 69 BC, by the pirates of Athenodorus, an ally of Mithridates. Since then, the island fell rapidly into decline and was gradually abandoned.

quarry.label: verified
quarry.says: Later it became a quarry: temple columns were burnt for lime and the houses left in ruins.
quote: Delos was turned into a quarry site with its temple columns burnt for lime, and its houses left in ruins.

abandoned.label: disputed
abandoned.says: Sources differ on when it was finally abandoned: UNESCO says uninhabited since the 7th century AD; Wikipedia says around the 8th century AD.
quote: it remained uninhabited since the 7th century AD
Delos was eventually abandoned around the eighth century AD.

excavations.label: verified
excavations.says: Excavations began in 1872 and are still going on.
quote: The excavations that started in 1872 and are still in progress
In 1872, the French School at Athens began excavating on Delos

kynthos.label: supported
kynthos.says: Mount Kynthos, which keeps its pre-Greek name, is crowned with a sanctuary of Zeus.
quote: Another site, retaining its Pre-Greek name Mount Cynthus, is crowned with a sanctuary of Zeus.

kynthos-view.label: supported
kynthos-view.says: From the top of Mount Kynthos there is a panoramic view of the surrounding islands.
quote: climb Mount Kynthos. From the top of the mountain you will have a panoramic view of the many surrounding islands.

cyclades.label: supported
cyclades.says: The Cyclades got their name in antiquity because they form a rough circle around Delos.
quote: The Cyclades received their name in antiquity because they form a rough circle (κύκλος/kyklos in Greek) round the sacred island of Delos.

proverb.label: supported
proverb.says: The Greeks had a proverb, 'you sing as if sailing into Delos', for someone happy and light-hearted.
quote: meaning you sing as if sailing into Delos in reference to someone who is happy, light-hearted, and enjoying himself.

parts.name: The Sacred Harbor
parts.stand: On the quay where the boat lands, facing inland toward the ruins.

paras.t: Welcome to Delos. It's a small island, but it's one of the most important places in all of Greek myth and history. Today the entire island is an archaeological site.
Before we walk: there's no protection from the sun out here, and the ground is rough, ancient stone. Wear a hat, watch your feet, and drink plenty of water as you go.

Nobody lives here now. Overnight stays are forbidden, and the only residents are security staff and archaeologists. UNESCO added Delos to the World Heritage List in 1990. Digging began in 1872, and it's still going on.

From this harbor, look for three cone-shaped hills. They once marked land sacred to a goddess, probably Athena. And near the harbor, in the paving of the old Agora of the Competaliasts, you can still find the holes where posts held up the market awnings.

parts.name: The Sanctuary of Apollo
parts.stand: Walk inland along the Sacred Way into the sanctuary, among the temple foundations.

paras.t: This was Apollo's sanctuary. It drew pilgrims from all over Greece, and around it Delos grew into a prosperous trading port.

People were living on Delos as far back as the third millennium BC. Apollo's sanctuary was here at least from the 9th century BC. Its high point came in the Archaic and Classical periods, when all of Greece came to share it. There are three temples to Apollo here.

Look beside the Temple of the Delians. A colossal statue of Apollo once stood there, from the 6th century BC. Parts of the upper body and hips still lie on the spot. One hand is in the island's museum. A foot is in the British Museum.
Every four years, in May, Delos held a great feast, with athletic, horse and music contests, dances, plays and banquets. It ran until 316 BC.

This is also where the Delian League began, in 478 BC: an alliance of Greek cities, somewhere between 150 and 330 of them, led by Athens, to keep fighting Persia. They met right here in the temple. To seal it, members dropped lumps of iron into the sea, a sign that the alliance was meant to be permanent.

The league's shared treasury was kept here too, until 454 BC, when Pericles moved it to Athens. Athens spent the money on its navy, and on art and buildings for the city. What began as an alliance came to be called the Athenian Empire.

The Athenians also wanted the island ritually pure. In the 6th century BC, the tyrant Pisistratus had every grave in sight of the temple dug up and moved. In the fifth century BC the whole island was cleared of the dead. And a decree said no one could be buried here, or give birth here. In Classical and Hellenistic times, the cemetery of Delos lay across the narrow channel, on the island of Rhenia.

parts.name: The Terrace of the Lions
parts.stand: At the Terrace of the Lions, facing the row of marble lions.

paras.t: Here are the famous lions of Delos. The people of Naxos gave this terrace to Apollo shortly before 600 BC. There were once nine to twelve of these crouching, snarling marble guardians along the Sacred Way.

One thing to know: these are exact copies. The north wind was wearing the marble away, so the originals were moved into the museum, and replicas took their place out here. Only seven of the original lions survive.
Picture the whole row, like an Egyptian avenue of sphinxes. And one of the missing lions? It was carried off, and today it stands over the main gate of the Venetian Arsenal.

parts.name: The Sacred Lake
parts.stand: Beside the round, dry hollow of the Sacred Lake.

paras.t: This round hollow was the Sacred Lake. And here, myth says, Leto gave birth to the twins Apollo and Artemis, after a long, hard labor.

The myth goes like this. Leto was pregnant by Zeus, and Zeus's wife Hera was jealous. Hera ordered every land on earth to turn Leto away. But Delos, the story goes, wasn't joined to the mainland or fixed to the sea floor. It didn't count as land. So it could take her in.

For nine days and nine nights, the myth says, she suffered near this lake. The goddess of childbirth, Eileithyia, was kept away, up on Olympus with Hera. On the ninth day the messenger goddess Iris won her over with a necklace and brought her here.

According to a Homeric hymn, the island had been floating until then, and now it was anchored to the ocean floor. The newborn Apollo threw off his swaddling clothes, bathed the universe in light, and began walking with his lyre and his bow.
Like most myths, this one comes in versions. In some, Artemis was born first, on another island called Ortygia. One local legend even put Apollo's birth in Boeotia, on the mainland.
Why is it dry? The caretakers keep it that way on purpose, to stop malaria mosquitoes from breeding.

parts.name: The merchant town
parts.stand: Among the walls of the ancient houses, on the paved lanes of the old town.

paras.t: Now the other Delos: a boom town. After 167 BC Delos became a free port, and the trade of the eastern Mediterranean poured in. An ancient writer called it the greatest commercial center of the whole world.

Rich merchants, bankers and ship-owners settled here and built luxurious houses, decorated with frescoes and mosaic floors. Look for the House of Dionysus, named for its mosaic of the god riding a panther, and the House of the Dolphins, with its mosaic of erotes riding dolphins.

There is a darker side, and we should say it plainly. Roman traders came here to buy tens of thousands of slaves. Delos became the center of the slave trade, with the largest slave market in the region.

People came from everywhere, and they brought their gods. There were temples to Sarapis, Isis and Anubis, to Syrian gods, and even a synagogue near the stadium. Exactly who worshiped in it, scholars have debated; it was once believed to be Samaritan. Inscriptions do record a community calling itself the Israelites on Delos, who made offerings to Mount Gerizim. Delos is also where an inscription honoring Herod the Great, King of Judaea, was found, and another honoring his son, Herod Antipas.

parts.name: The museum
parts.stand: Inside the site museum, in front of the original lions.

paras.t: Here, out of the wind, are the original Naxian lions.
The museum is known for its statues from across the site, but it doesn't hold everything. A large share of the finds from Delos is in the National Archaeological Museum in Athens.

parts.name: The end of Delos, and the view
parts.stand: On Mount Kynthos, or wherever you can look back over the ruins to the sea.

paras.t: All this wealth made Delos a target. It was attacked and looted twice: in 88 BC by Mithridates, King of Pontus, and in 69 BC by pirates allied with him. After that it declined, and was slowly abandoned.

Later the island became a quarry. Temple columns were burnt for lime, and the houses were left in ruins. When did the last people leave? Nobody knows exactly: UNESCO says the island was uninhabited from the 7th century AD, Wikipedia says abandoned around the 8th.

If you have the time and the legs for it, climb Mount Kynthos. It's crowned with a sanctuary of Zeus, and from the top you get a panoramic view of the islands around you. The Cyclades took their name from the rough circle they form around Delos.
The path up can be rough, and there's no shade. Go slowly, and watch your footing on the way down.
The ancient Greeks had a saying for someone happy and light-hearted: you sing as if sailing into Delos. People still make this crossing today. I hope you sail home singing.
